items.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023
items.q: On Harry James I had Buddy Rich for four years. Then when he left Sonny Payne — I mean Louie Bellson came on for a couple of months, then Sonny Payne came.

ctx.x: Did you ever have any sort of philosophical disagreements with the drummers about how things are supposed to go?

No. I didn’t have much choice. I had really good luck with drummers. On Harry James I had Buddy Rich for four years. Then when he left Sonny Payne — I mean Louie Bellson came on for a couple of months, then Sonny Payne came. So I couldn’t argue much with those three. No, it was just a natural feel. The first night I played I flew out from New York and went to Lake Tahoe and played. Sat down and played and you know, was comfortable with Buddy right away. And he was comfortable with me right away, luckily, ‘cause…
I have it from an inside source that he used to massage your shoulders or something afterwards, to sort of help you get through the night.
